This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondent No.1 & 2 under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for the relief of compensation.
SCCH-5 2.

The brief facts of the case is as under; That on 09.05.2023 at about 7.00 p.m. she had been proceeding as a pillion rider on motor cycle bearing Reg. No.AP-9-KA-3810 being ridden by her husband near Mahasamudram Toll Plaza, on Palamaner - Chittoor Road, NH-69, Bangarupalam Mandal, at that time, a lorry bearing Reg. No.TN-61-E-5006 came in rash and negligent manner and dashed against motor cycle on which petitioner was travelling, due to the said impact, petitioner fell down and sustained injuries.

Immediately after the accident, she was shifted to Government Hospital, Chittoor, thereafter shifted to CMC Hospital, Ranipeta, wherein she took treatment as inpatient and left upper limb of the petitioner got amputated.
Petitioner has spent a sum of Rs.5,00,000/- hospitalization and medicine charges.
SCCH-5 3.
Prior to the accident, she was hale and healthy, aged about 29 years, working as tailor, thereby earning Rs.25,000/- p.m.

Due to the injuries sustained in the accident, she has lost her left hand and not able to do her day-to-day activities, so that, she has engaged an attendant, she has also suffered lot of mental stress and agone and lost her earning capacity.

The accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the lorry bearing Reg. No.TN-61-E-5006 by its driver and Bangarpalem Urban Police have registered a case in crime No.107/2023 for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 338 of IPC.

The 1st Respondent is the insurer and respondent No.2 is owner of the said offending lorry, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- to the petitioner with interest at the rate of 12% p.a. SCCH-5 4.
In pursuance of service of notice, the Respondent No.1/insurer has appeared before the tribunal through counsel and filed written statement by denying entire averments of the petition.
Further submitted that, insurance policy is issued in respect of lorry bearing Reg. No.TN-61-E-5006 and its liability is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
Further respondent No.1 is entitled to seek protection available under Sec.56, 66, 147, 149(2) and 170 of M.V.Act.

8. Issue No.1:-
The petitioner inorder to prove her case, she herself examined as PW-1 and in her chief- examination evidence, she has reiterated petition averments.
Though she has been elaborately cross- examined by the Respondent No.1 counsel, but nothing is brought on record to disbelieve the evidence of the petitioner.
9. Further to substantiate her case, petitioner has examined Dr.Chidanand K.J.C. as PW-2, who examined the petitioner has stated that, petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.

10. Apart from the oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked copy of FIR as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint marked as Ex.P.2, copy of form No.54 marked as Ex.P.3, SCCH-5 copy of MLC marked as Ex.P.4, copy of Sketch marked as Ex.P.5, copy of Final Report marked as Ex.P.6.
11.
Per contra, ARTO, Kanchipuram is examined as RW-1 and exhibited authorization letter marked as Ex.R.1, copy of letter marked as Ex.R.2, copy of DL Extract marked as Ex.R.3.
further Legal Executive of respondent No.1 is examined as RW-2 and exhibited authorization letter marked as Ex.R.4 and copy of policy marked as Ex.R.5.
Further except above evidence, respondent No.1 has not taken any endeavors to disprove the petitioner's case about non-causing of the accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.

Since in the absence of iota of evidence, I have no hesitation to believe the case of the petitioner about causing of the injuries to the petitioner out of the accident held on 09.05.2023 at about 7.00 p.m. when she was proceeding as a pillion SCCH-5 rider on motor cycle bearing Reg. No.AP-39-KA-3810 near Mahasamudram Toll Plaza, on Palamaner - Chittoor Road, NH-69, Bangarupalam Mandal.
In the absence of iota of evidence, the arguments advanced by the petitioner's counsel are helpful to the case of the petitioner.
12. The police papers speaks that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of the driver of the lorry bearing Reg. No.TN-61-E-5006.

Under such circumstances, considering the said evidence and believing the evidence of the petitioner, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, petitioner has proved the above issue No.1 in her favour.
Accordingly I have answered above Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
13. Issue No.2:-
As per the evidence of the petitioner, she had sustained crush injury of left upper SCCH-5 limb, traumatic total amputation of left upper limb, T2 spinous process fracture.

Further during the course of arguments, petitioner counsel Sri.AA argued that, the Doctor has given 90% disability and left hand amputation was done and she was doing tailoring business earlier to accident and earlier avocation was lost due to amputation and LMV DL holder also have got capacity to drive HGV and RW-1 evidence supports the case of the petitioner and there is no mention about LMV and HGV vehicle in Ex.R.3 document and counsel prays to allow the petition by relying above rulings.

Ofcourse in the above said rulings, the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held that,
i) incase of violation of any conditions of policy, the principle of pay and recovery will attracts SCCH-5 ii) in any cases, the amputation were done, then 100% disability should be considered etc.,
25.

On the other hand, respondent counsel argued that as per Ex.R.3 document, the driver of the offending vehicle Dinesh L. is only having LMV DL and he has no capacity to drive the heavy vehicle and as per the evidence of RW-1 upto 7500 kgs weight, the LMV licence holder is capable to drive the vehicle and pay and recovery principle will not attracts to the case, because the accident was held after amendment to the M.V.Act and against the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka judgment passed in MFA No.202104/2024 review is pending before the Hon'ble High Court and judgments of other courts are not supports the petitioner case and only respondent No.2 alone is liable to pay the compensation and prays to dismiss the petition.
SCCH-5 26.

On perusal of evidence of RW-1, the official of RTO Office, Kanchipuram, she categorically stated that, Dinesh L. i.e., respondent No.2 is having only LMV licence and she placed Ex.R.3 document.

As per the said document, the said Dinesh L. had LMV - TR licence issued by the Tamil Nadu State Kanchipuram RTO and it is valid from 15.07.2011 to 14.07.2031, but admittedly in the alleged accident i.e., the vehicle of respondent No.1 was involved i.e., TN-61-E-5006 i.e., Lorry, so the weight of the above vehicle is above 7500 kgs and respondent No.2 who is not capable to drive the said vehicle, because as per the evidence of RW-1, RW-2 and Ex.R.3 documents, he possessed only LMV, so he has no capacity and right to drive the HGV and hence respondent No.1 is not liable to pay the compensation, because respondent No.2 being the owner of the vehicle SCCH-5 driven the vehicle without possessing HGV licence and he has no valid licence, as such, who is liable to pay the compensation and further Investigation Officer has filed charge sheet against Dinesh L. for the alleged offences.

Accordingly, the rulings submitted by the petitioner have not supports the case,
because the facts and circumstances involved in the said rulings are entirely different from the present set of facts.
Accordingly, as discussed above, respondent No.2 being the owner is liable to deposit above said compensation amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.
Accordingly I answer Issue No.2 partly in affirmative.

27. Issue No.3: For the reasons assigned to Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
::ORDER::
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.
SCCH-5 The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.14,64,147/- (Rupees Fourteen Lakhs Sixty Four Thousand One Hundred Forty Seven Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.2 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.
The Petitioner is entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through e-payment directly to his account on furnishing the Bank A/c details along with address proof and remaining 40% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in his name.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

Considering the fracture injury sustained by the petitioner and disability as stated by the Doctor and on account of the discomfort SCCH-5 and unhappiness the claimant has to undergo in her future life, it is just and proper to award a sum of Rs.50,000/- towards loss of amenities.
Therefore,
considering the materials on record, it is just and proper to award a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- towards cost of artificial limb and its maintenance.
The above said all SCCH-5 compensation heads are considered as per the recent rulings of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India reported in Civil Appeal Nos.9070-9071 of 2022 in between Mohd. Sabeer @ Shabir Hussain V/s. Regional Manager, U.P.State Road Transport Corporation.
